status_summary: The work-requirement half is law and operative: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) raised the SNAP time-limit age for adults without dependents to 64, narrowed the child exemption to children under 14, removed exemptions for veterans, homeless people and former foster youth, and limited area waivers, effective on enactment, with USDA guidance in September and October 2025. The same law also requires Medicaid community engagement (80 hours a month) for expansion adults, implemented by a CMS interim final rule published 2026-06-03 (effective 2026-07-31; states must comply by 2027-01-01). The marriage-penalty half is not addressed in the sources read: a coalition letter to the House Speaker on 2026-01-06 treats welfare marriage-penalty reform as a future reconciliation goal, and a July 2026 report describes a bill to remove a marriage penalty in the state and local tax deduction cap, which is a proposal, not law.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed; its SNAP section 10102 raises the able-bodied adult work requirement upper age to 64, limits the dependent exemption to children under 14, removes exemptions for veterans, homeless people and former foster youth, and limits area waivers, effective on enactment.
The same law adds section 71119, a Medicaid community engagement requirement for certain adults.
USDA issues guidance on the revised adult exemptions under the new law (ages 18 to 64, child exemption under 14, removal of veteran, homeless and former foster youth exemptions).

The U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island issues a temporary restraining order halting USDA's planned early termination of certain SNAP time-limit waivers; USDA guidance of 2026-02-26 later keeps the affected waivers through their original end dates.

A coalition of conservative and faith-based groups writes to the House Speaker asking that a reconciliation package address welfare marriage penalties and phase-outs; the letter identifies no enacted change to marriage penalties in 2025 or 2026.
timeline.source: Coalition letter hosted by Rep. Grothman

timeline.event: CMS publishes the Medicaid community engagement interim final rule (effective 2026-07-31): expansion adults ages 19 to 64 must show 80 hours a month of work, service, a work program, education or equivalent income, with listed exemptions, and states must comply by 2027-01-01.
Trade press reports a new bill that would double the state and local tax deduction cap for joint filers, described as eliminating a marriage penalty in that cap; it is a proposal and not law.

title: Eliminate marriage penalties in welfare and taxes; add work requirements for food stamps
uncertainties: The statute text of Public Law 119-21 was not read directly for this record; SNAP changes come from the USDA memo and the Medicaid section number from the c14-05 record and the CMS rule. Whether the law changed any marriage penalties inside the tax code (for example in deductions, credits or phase-outs) was not systematically examined: a limited search found only advocacy briefs, a coalition letter and one trade-press bill report, none of which show an enacted elimination, so the absence of change is an inference from limited evidence. The Foreword's phrase food stamps maps to SNAP. The Ballotpedia item is a secondary summary. Related records c10-01 and c14-05 have more detail on each program. The SNAP time limit now reaches adults through age 64, per the USDA October 2025 guidance. The Rhode Island order was read only through a secondary summary.
